newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Czech ministry plans further big selloffs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Czech ministry plans further big selloffs.

text.p: The further privatisation of shares in major Czech banks and industries is to get a jump start under a finance ministry plan expected to be debated by the full cabinet later this month.

The ministry, directed by the cabinet in April to accelerate the pace of privatisation to help a lagging economy, said on Tuesday that it planned to begin the further selloff this year of shares in two of the four largest banks Komercni Banka a.s. and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s..

Igor Fojtik, the director of the ministry's privatisation department, also told Reuters that the further privatisation of shares in the largest retail savings bank, Ceska Sporitelna was not planned for this year but possibly for 1998.

"This year, the beginning of privatisation of (16 regional gas and electricity) distribution companies, CSOB and Komercni Banka, three coal mining companies, (pharmaceutical producer) Leciva, and the partial privatisation of (radio transmitter Ceske Radiokomunikace, and tin producer Valcovny Plechu is planned," Fojtik said.
"We are not expecting that Sporitelna would go through (further) privatisation this year. That will evidently come next year," he added.

The government is nearing a decision on a tender offering about a one-third stake in the third largest Czech bank, Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. with Nomura Intl. and Dutch bank ING competing as finalists.
The new finance ministry plans came as the beleagured centre-right government promised to speed up privatisations to build more efficiency into the country's slowing economy.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's government, once seen as a leading force in post-Communist privatisation, has come under intense pressure as an economic slowdown has been blamed, in part, on state control of banks and investment companies which have not forced needed restructuring in industry.
Last week, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, who received the original directive on privatisation from the cabinet in April, was sacked and replaced by Education Minister Ivan Pilip.
There was no sign that the plan had been affected by the change in ministers.
The CSOB and Komercni privatisations would entail partial stakes being sold through public tenders with other stakes placed on domestic and foreign capital markets.
The government's long-awaited privatisation of the 16 regional energy distributors has been delayed several times.
The latest ministry plan calls for the sell-off of a 15 percent stake in each energy distribution firm through public tenders this year, with the remainder being sold in 1998.

Fojtik said any consideration of privatising another stake before the year 2000 in fixed-line monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. would not be made, remaining in line with the government's previous long-term plan.
Fojtik said the three coal mining companies to be privatised would be Mostecka Uhelna, Severoceske Doly, and Sokolovska Uhelna, but not OKD a.s., another of the largest mining firms.
He said further consideration of OKD's privatisation would come possibly "sometime around 1998 and 1999".

Fojtik added that the further privatisation of the largest electricity utility CEZ a.s. would have to wait until the completion of the Temelin nuclear power station. So would further privatisation of the project's general contractor Skoda Praha a.s..
Temelin is not expected to go on stream until 1999 at the earliest.
"At CEZ we expect the construction of Temelin and then we can consider other privatisation steps. That also means Skoda Praha as the general supplier," Fojtik said.
Details of finance ministry privatisation plans:
* Komercni Banka a.s. and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s.:
Partial placement of shares on foreign and domestic stock markets, plus partial stakes sold in each bank by public tender.
* Savings bank Ceska Sporitelna a.s.: further privatisation possibly in 1998.
* Regional gas and electricity distribution companies (16 in total): 15 percent stakes sold in public tender this year, with the remaining state stakes sold in 1998.
* Ceske Radiokomunikace a.s.: Rights issue offering 19 percent to current shareholders.
* Leciva a.s. pharmaceuticals: Direct sale of 66 percent stake to management.
* CEZ a.s., Skoda Praha a.s.: further privatisation waiting on completion of Temelin nuclear power station (expected in 1999 at the earliest)
* Coal minining companies Mostecka Uhelna, Severoceske Doly, Sokolovska Uhelna: 10 percent stake sold to management, the remainder in public tenders.
* Tin maker Valcovna Plechu: direct sale to Czech steel makers Nova Hut or Trinecke Zelezarny
